lastCompletedStory.title: Replace non-null assertions in the fixture-matrix test with a narrowing guard

nextStoryContext: The 'oracle-lint-cases.txt fixture matrix' test (test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts, 'every row classifies as its recorded ok/flag expectation') no longer uses `rule!.test(command!)` / `expected!`. It now destructures each parsed row as `const [ruleName, expected, command] = row` and throws a named Error before use: one guard for a malformed row (any of the three fields undefined, message includes JSON.stringify(row)), a second guard when RULES.find() returns no match for ruleName (message includes the offending ruleName and JSON.stringify(row)), mirroring the pre-existing `findGrepRule()` helper's `if (!rule) throw new Error(...)` idiom already used elsewhere in this file. Verified live: temporarily fed the guard an unknown rule name via `bun -e` and confirmed it throws the named Error with the row payload, not a bare TypeError. All 71 tests in the file still pass (same verdicts), full suite is 5243 pass / 0 fail, and `bun run check:all` is green end-to-end (typecheck, test, embed-vendor, lint, file-size, debt-markers, version-skips, coverage, dead-code, dup, ci-parity, agents-md, test-sleeps all ok) -- no ceiling/floor raises were needed. No src/ changes; test-only story. Pure mechanical refactor, no new reusable pattern worth a patterns.md bullet.
